```{r}
#| include: false
cards <- yaml::read_yaml("caveats.yml", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")$categories
n_cards <- sum(vapply(cards, \(c) length(c$cards), 1L))
```

A checklist of the mistakes that most often make a chart mislead or confuse, as **`r n_cards` flash cards** in
`r length(cards)` groups. Read the title, decide what the problem is and how you would fix it, then **open the card**.
Use **Practise** to be dealt the cards one at a time; the ones you mark *Review again* come back first.

Most of these points are taught in [Best Practices](best_practices.qmd), [Matching Data to Plots](plot_data.qmd)
and the ggplot2 modules; each card links to where. The list of topics follows the caveats collection of
[data-to-viz.com](https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveats.html) by Yan Holtz and Conor Healy, where many cards have a
longer illustrated page (the "data-to-viz" link on the card). The original illustrated flash cards are at
[dataviz-inspiration.com/caveats](https://www.dataviz-inspiration.com/caveats)
([source](https://github.com/holtzy/dataviz-caveat-flashcards), CC BY-NC 4.0, so they are linked here, not copied).
The wording and the R code here are our own.

::: {.cv-toolbar}
[All]{.cv-filter .active data-cat="all"}
```{r}
#| output: asis
for (c in cards) cat(sprintf('[%s (%d)]{.cv-filter data-cat="%s"}\n', c$name, length(c$cards), c$name))
```
[🃏 Practise]{.cv-practise}
:::

::: {.cv-practice-box style="display:none"}
:::

```{r}
#| output: asis
esc <- function(x) gsub(">", "&gt;", gsub("<", "&lt;", gsub("&", "&amp;", x)))
for (c in cards) {
  cat(sprintf('\n## %s {.cv-heading data-cat="%s"}\n\n::: {.cv-grid data-cat="%s"}\n', c$name, c$name, c$name))
  for (k in c$cards) {
    cat(sprintf('\n::: {.cv-card data-cat="%s"}\n<details>\n<summary>%s</summary>\n\n', c$name, esc(k$title)))
    cat(sprintf('**Problem.** %s\n\n**Fix.** %s\n\n', k$problem, k$fix))
    if (!is.null(k$code)) cat("```r\n", k$code, "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
    links <- c(if (!is.null(k$course)) sprintf("[In the course: %s](../%s)", k$course[[2]], k$course[[1]]),
               if (!is.null(k$dtv)) sprintf("[data-to-viz](%s)", k$dtv))
    if (length(links)) cat(paste(links, collapse = " · "), "\n\n")
    cat("</details>\n:::\n")
  }
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

## Self-check quiz

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../assets/quiz.R")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("cv1", "A chart shows the mean SBP of two arms as bars with error bars, the y-axis starting at 120 mmHg. How many caveats does it break?",
         c("None: the error bars make it an honest chart", "One: the error bars alone are wrong", "Two: the cut axis and the bar of means", "One: just the axis start is wrong"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Bars must start at zero, and a bar of the mean hides the data; show points with the mean and its CI instead.")
quiz_mcq("cv2", "You map dengue cases (counts) per block. What should you map instead, and why?",
         c("Cases per 100,000, so population does not drive it", "The log of the counts, to compress the colour scale", "Cases per km², so that large blocks look smaller", "The rank of each count, so classes have equal size"), answer = 1,
         explain = "A count map mostly shows where people live; a rate shows the risk.")
quiz_mcq("cv3", "Twenty ward lines overlap on one time-series chart. Which fix keeps every ward visible?",
         c("Give each of the wards its own bright, saturated colour", "Small multiples, each ward over the rest in grey", "A 3D chart with one ward per depth level", "A dual y-axis for the larger and smaller wards"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Small multiples with the other series in grey keep context and make each line readable.")
quiz_mcq("cv4", "Change in SBP from baseline (negative and positive) is shown on a map. Which palette fits?",
         c("A rainbow palette from red to violet", "A single-hue palette from light to dark blue", "A qualitative palette with one hue per block", "A diverging palette with white at zero"), answer = 4,
         explain = "Data with a meaningful zero need two hues meeting at a neutral midpoint.")
```
